title: Delirium on Intensive Care Units. How does an educational intervention affect Delirium?
summary: Does an interprofessional education program in intensive care units, combined with education of relatives, reduce the incidence of delirium?
conditions: Delirium, not induced by alcohol and other psychoactive substances

interventions.name:
- interprofessional education program for staff (6 months, 1/week) 
- family education (face-to-face, 1x 30 min. before visiting + 15 min. bedside education, posters, flyers, digital information)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients‘ attributes
- Age >18 years
- ≥ 3 days on ICU/IMC
- relatives available
- no common diseases with corresponding symptoms that meet the delirium screening criteria (e.g. severe dementia)
- no current diseases with symptoms overlapping delirium screening criteria (e.g. delirium of different etiology, encephalopathy)

Relatives’ attributes
- Age >18 years
- Frequent visitors (at least every second day)
- Sufficient German language skills 
Consent given
Exclusion criteria:
Patients‘ attributes
- do not conform with aforementioned inclusion criteria 
- mechanical ventilation during the entire ICU stay (no ICDSC screening of non-ventilated patient throughout the whole stay possible: no clear assessment of patient orientation possible)

Relatives’ attributes
- Age <18 years
- infrequent visitors 
- insufficient German language skills 
- no consent given
sponsor: Kooperation zwischen Universitätsmedizin Frankfurt, Philipps-Universität Marburg und Hochschule Fulda
